title: Be a warm day I fancy. Specially in these black clothes feel it more. Black conducts, reflects, (refracts is it?), the heat.
html_source:
Is this true? Let’s let The Straight Dope take this one away. First of all, it’s white clothing that reflects sunlight–but there’s a catch:

White clothing reflects sunlight, but also reflects internal heat back towards your body, so the net effect under identical conditions is less cooling than if you wore black.

Black clothing actually keeps you cooler, for reasons related to wind speed:

…black clothing absorbs sunlight and the heat radiating from your body, but if it is loose-fitting, and there is wind, the wind convects the heat away faster than it is absorbed.

The full breakdown is here. By the way, refraction of light is something totally different–that’s when light waves change direction due to a change in transmission medium, as from air to water. It’s what causes objects half-in, half-out of water to appear broken or distorted:

Bottom line: Bloom’s a smart guy, but he’s a little off base on this one.
